items.title: Mississauga residents back subway extension, but few confident it will actually be built
items.summary: A majority of Mississauga residents support bringing subway service to downtown, but a new survey suggests there is far less agreement over whether it should take priority over improved GO service. A survey of 1,000 Mississauga residents found 65 per cent support extending subway service to downtown Mississauga near Square One, while 20 per cent oppose the idea and 15 per cent are unsure. But when residents were asked to choose between a subway extension and all-day, two-way GO train service on the Milton line, the result was almost evenly divided. Forty-five per cent picked the subway as the better transit investment, while 44 per cent chose expanded Milton GO service. Another 11 per cent were unsure. The survey was conducted by Liaison Strategies between Oct. 2 and Oct. 4, shortly after the subway proposal was raised during the Mississauga mayoral campaign. The poll found an even bigger gap between support for the subway and confidence that it will actually be built. Only 19 per cent of respondents said they were very or somewhat confident a subway extension would eventually be constructed. Four per cent were very confident and 15 per cent somewhat confident. Meanwhile, 61 per cent said they were either not very or not at all confident the project would be built, while 20 per cent were unsure.

items.title: Loaded handgun and $16,000 in drugs seized as Mississauga man faces charges in Sarnia
items.summary: A 49-year-old Mississauga man is facing multiple drug and firearms charges after police seized a loaded handgun and an estimated $16,000 worth of drugs during a search in Sarnia. The Sarnia Police Service Drug Unit, with assistance from the Intelligence Unit and Emergency Response Team, executed a search warrant in the 1700 block of London Line on Oct. 6. 40 in Canadian currency. Officers also seized a loaded Taurus 9mm handgun and additional ammunition. Police have not released the accused’s name. The Mississauga man was arrested and charged with 11 offences, including possession of a prohibited firearm, possession of a firearm while prohibited from doing so, possession of ammunition while prohibited, and possession of a firearm without a licence. He is also charged with carrying a concealed firearm, carrying a weapon for a dangerous purpose, possession of cocaine for the purpose of trafficking and possession of methamphetamine for the purpose of trafficking. Police also laid an additional charge of possession of property obtained by crime.

items.title: Kenneth Law case: Families reveal the devastating toll in 'The Poison Seller'
items.summary: Mississauga’s Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to aiding suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to people around the world. A CBC investigation linked Law to at least 147 deaths, but the real number might never be known. The Poison Seller, a documentary from The Passionate Eye, examines the investigation that left families asking why police didn't halt his operations sooner, and the CBC’s Kelda Yuen sat down with the filmmaking team behind it. If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available. In Canada, you can call or text 988 to reach the Suicide Crisis Helpline. Kids Help Phone is available at 1-800-668-6868, or by texting 686868.

items.title: Drivers at Ridgeway Plaza nabbed by cops during Mississauga enforcement campaign
items.summary: Police issued more tickets for stunt driving, street racing and other serious offences at two Mississauga hot spots during a recent enforcement campaign than anywhere else in the region. Peel Regional Police officers visited Ridgeway Plaza (and nearby Auto Spa area) in the city’s west end 26 times to lay charges as part of their latest Project ERASE (Eliminating Racing Activities on Streets Everywhere) initiative, stats presented last week to the City of Mississauga’s Road Safety Committee show. Ridgeway Plaza has regularly attracted headlines since opening in 2022 related to excessive late-night noise, street racing, parking concerns and other issues. Police targeted specific areas in Mississauga and Brampton — the spots “that everybody’s been complaining about,” Peel police Const. Claudia D’Amico told committee members — during their most-recent Project ERASE campaign. The enforcement initiative ran from May 1 through the end of August and also included Ontario Provincial Police as well as municipal law enforcement agencies in Toronto, Durham, Halton and Hamilton. The Peel Regional Police numbers included enforcement action taken only in Mississauga and Brampton. In addition to Ridgeway Plaza, police officers on the hunt for dangerous and illegal driving behaviour conducted enforcement on 22 occasions in the Financial Plaza area in north Meadowvale, information presented to the committee showed. That part of the city is also known for illegal street racing and other dangerous driving, police have said.

items.title: Nearly 150 Residents Turn Out to Grill Five Ward 3 Candidates on Taxes and Bloor Street Redesign
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, nearly 150 residents attended a Ward 3 candidates meeting on Oct. 5, where five council hopefuls, Kim Pines, Mendi Kabashi, Chris Fonseca, Arshad Hashmi and Stjepan Vukovic, fielded questions on property taxes, the Bloor Street redesign project and public safety in the Applewood and Rockwood neighbourhoods. The event was co-hosted by the Applewood Hills and Heights Residents' Association and the Rockwood Residents' Association, and was held at Sts. Martha and Mary Parish Catholic Church. Resident Pedro Coronado, who has lived in the ward for nearly 10 years, told the outlet he already knew who he wanted to vote for before the meeting, but said attending solidified his decision. Coronado said he voted differently in the last municipal election, explaining that rising costs over the past five years changed his thinking this time around. Mississauga.com reports sisters Lorraine Katanik and Kathy Klas arrived undecided and left with enough information to make up their minds. The meeting is one of several ward-level candidate forums being held across Mississauga ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election.

items.title: Mississauga Rents Dip to $2,337 in September as Two-Year National Downturn Continues
items.summary: According to a report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation, Mississauga's average rent fell slightly to $2,337 in September, down from $2,365 in August, keeping the city as Canada's 13th most expensive rental market. The report found Canada is now in its second straight year of falling rents, which Urbanation president Shaun Hildebrand called the longest rental downturn the country has seen in recent history. Hildebrand said the correction has mainly been driven by a surge in new housing supply, and that markets like Toronto and Vancouver are now moving past their supply peak. He said rents in those cities have started trending higher over the past six months, with annual declines narrowing significantly as renters return to the market. Nearby, Halifax recorded an average rent of $2,324, just below Mississauga, while Vaughan came in higher at $2,363. The report noted the slowdown fits a typical seasonal pattern, following four straight monthly increases from April through July before rents eased again in August and September.

items.title: Three Leading Mayoral Candidates Back Breaking Mississauga Away From Peel Region
items.summary: According to Insauga, three of Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates said at Monday night's debate that they still want the city to split from Peel Region, despite the Ontario government shelving that plan nearly three years ago. Asked a yes-or-no question on whether Mississauga should remain part of Peel, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla all answered that Canada's seventh-largest city should go it alone rather than stay grouped with Brampton and Caledon. Incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish was not on stage for the debate, but Insauga reports she has repeatedly said she also supports Mississauga's independence from the region. Parrish raised the idea again in June 2025 amid an ongoing dispute between Mississauga and its regional counterparts, suggesting that friction alone justified revisiting a breakup. The province had told Mississauga officials in mid-2023 that it would let the city separate, only to reverse course that December after more than three decades of the city pushing for the split. Insauga notes the debate's yes-or-no format was part of a series of rapid-fire questions put to the four major candidates.

items.title: Ministry of Labour Fines Gay Lea Foods $80,000 Over Guelph Plant Fall Injury
items.summary: According to the Ontario Ministry of Labour, Gay Lea Foods Co-operative Limited has been fined $80,000 after pleading guilty in Provincial Offences Court in Guelph on Sept. 18 to a charge under the Occupational Health and Safety Act. The ministry said a worker was injured in March 2025 after falling from the top of a milk transport truck while collecting samples at the company's Guelph dairy processing plant. Workers normally reach the sampling hatches using an elevated gantry fitted with steps and guardrails, but the ministry said some workers would instead step onto the top of the truck to reach a second hatch without repositioning the gantry. On March 23, 2025, the ministry said a milk receiver stepped from the gantry onto the truck and was no longer protected by the guardrail system, resulting in the fall. The ministry said Gay Lea Foods failed to properly instruct and supervise workers on the safe use of the hatch access system. Gay Lea Foods, Ontario's largest farmer-owned dairy co-operative, operated out of Mississauga for nearly two decades before relocating to Etobicoke near Toronto Pearson Airport in 2025.
